prose: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Fiddler AI - which monitors AI agents - for roughly $400M, and Dreadnode, an automated AI security-testing tool, for about $95M, mostly in cash, per the Wall Street Journal. The deals land as companies deploy AI agents faster than security teams can establish controls: agent observability and adversarial testing are becoming security-stack line items.
highlights: CrowdStrike buys Fiddler AI (~$400M) and Dreadnode (~$95M), mostly cash, per WSJ
Agent monitoring + automated AI red-teaming consolidated into a major security vendor
Context: enterprises deploying agents faster than security teams can govern them
basis: Error cache: WSJ paywall/bot-block. Written from the Techmeme headline and James Rundle's lede; figures from the headline.
